title: UbuntuGuard: A Culturally-Grounded Policy Benchmark for Equitable AI Safety in African Languages
findings: Models exhibited one of their highest error rates in the 'Culture and Religion' domain (6.27%), suggesting they struggle significantly with adjudicating highly contextual or subjective content where safety boundaries are dependent on local cultural nuance.

measurement_description: The benchmark measures the ability of guardian models to adhere to culturally-grounded safety policies in dialogues related to religion. This includes adjudicating highly contextual and subjective content, avoiding misinformation, and providing nuanced responses in specific religious contexts, such as discussions about Christian pastoring in Nigeria.
